The FAA approved the use of the technology across the full 10,000-foot-long and 150-foot-wide runway, making the project a significant step for the use of carbon-capture concrete in airfield construction.Runway 5R-23L is an important part of Indianapolis International Airport because it handles most of the airport's cargo operations as well as a substantial amount of commercial airline traffic. The Sustainable Infrastructure report describes it as a 150-foot-wide, 10,000-foot-long runway forming part of the airport's southeast-side facilities.The reconstruction replaced the existing pavement with full-depth Portland cement concrete and included changes to the taxiway, drainage, markings, signs, lighting and navigation equipment. Kimley-Horn reported that the wider project reconstructed more than 450,000 square yards of concrete pavement while adding new LED lighting, signs, a firefighting water line and upgraded navigation aids.The pavement was also designed with longevity in mind. Engineering News-Record reported that the existing runway, which was about 30 years old, was expected to have a 40-year life after reconstruction rather than the previous 20-year expectation. An analysis led the project team to increase the pavement depth by an inch.Much of the material removed during construction did not simply become waste. The Indianapolis Airport Authority said the existing runway concrete would be crushed on site and recycled into the new project.Kimley-Horn later reported that the wider project diverted nearly 690,000 tons of waste from landfill, achieving a diversion rate of more than 99%. Crushed concrete was reused as aggregate base material and pipe bedding, reducing the need to transport replacement materials.Other materials were also put to use. Signs and lighting removed from the project were transferred for reuse at other airports in Indiana. The project also used recycled non-potable water for activities including dust control, compaction and irrigation, reducing the use of drinking-quality water by 50%, according to Kimley-Horn.These measures made material reuse a major part of the reconstruction rather than treating sustainability as something limited to the concrete mix.The runway project also incorporated renewable energy. The Indianapolis Airport Authority said the reconstruction included a 1,000-kilowatt direct-current solar photovoltaic system along with battery storage.The Sustainable Infrastructure report estimated that the solar installation would generate 1,552,341 kilowatt-hours of electricity each year, compared with an estimated 419,060 kilowatt-hours required by the project itself. The surplus electricity was intended to serve other airfield electrical systems beyond the immediate construction area.Kimley-Horn reported that the completed project also included a 10-acre photovoltaic solar array and two battery storage systems. These systems were designed to supply power to the Midfield Vault and one of the airport's aircraft rescue and firefighting facilities.LED lighting and signage were another part of the work. Kimley-Horn projected that the updated system could reduce operational energy consumption by 31% compared with the previous system.The combination of carbon capture, material reuse, renewable energy and other measures helped the project receive the Envision Platinum Award from the Institute for Sustainable Infrastructure.The Indianapolis Airport Authority said the $190 million project was the first airfield project in the world to receive the Platinum designation.According to the Indianapolis Airport Authority, the project was expected to create more than 2,700 jobs, while economic analysis found that every dollar spent on the reconstruction would generate another $0.80 in economic activity in Marion County.Kimley-Horn described the project as a multi-year effort shaped by extensive coordination because Runway 5R-23L sits beside the airport's major FedEx cargo operation. Construction had to be phased carefully to limit disruption while maintaining safe airport operations.
Article Summary: Indianapolis International Airport rebuilt its 10,000-foot-long Runway 5R-23L with concrete designed to capture and permanently store carbon dioxide inside the pavement. The $190 million reconstruction project introduced carbon-capture technology to an entire airport runway after receiving approval from the Federal Aviation Administration. It combined the new concrete system with recycled construction materials, renewable energy and upgrades intended to improve the runway.

Article Title: Trump says he deserves 8 Nobel Peace Prizes, calls award ‘forever discredited’
Article Text:
‘Eight Nobel prizes’: Trump slams Norway, says peace award has been ‘discredited’

US President Donald Trump on Friday criticised Norway for not awarding him the Nobel Peace Prize, claiming he deserved the honour eight times for the wars he said he had settled.Addressing a rally in Syracuse, Trump also claimed to have saved 50 million lives by preventing India and Pakistan from going to war.“The United States of America, represented by me as your president, should have received the Nobel peace prize, but didn’t. And this is an indelible stain on the country of Norway, and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision,” Trump said.“The Nobel peace prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilisation. We will not forget, Norway, that you didn’t give this prize,” the US President added.Trump then listed the conflicts he claimed to have resolved, adding that he was working to end two more, involving Iran and the Russia-Ukraine war.“We will not forget Norway, that you didn't give this prize with the greatest record in history — eight wars, we should have had 8 Nobel Prizes for each war— but that you didn't give the Nobel Prize for Peace to the United States of America,” he added.“Additionally, I stopped Iran from having a nuclear weapon and blowing up the entire Middle East and ultimately far beyond the Middle East, including Europe, perhaps the US and I saved more lives than anyone in history,” Trump said.The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to South African former UN human rights chief Navi Pillay, whom Trump dismissed as someone “nobody ever heard of”.“The Nobel Prize was given out today (Friday) to a liberal person who works at the United Nations, who nobody has ever heard of. I've never heard of the person, but congratulations anyway,” Trump said.Pillay, 85, is a South African-born jurist and former UN human rights chief who won the Nobel Peace Prize for her work promoting international law. She served as an International Criminal Court (ICC) judge from 2003 to 2008 and later chaired a UN commission that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, a finding strongly rejected by Israel.Four US presidents have received the Nobel Peace Prize: Theodore Roosevelt, Woodrow Wilson, Jimmy Carter and Barack Obama. Obama won the award in 2009, his first year in office.Trump has repeatedly criticised Obama’s win, arguing that he “got a prize for doing nothing”.Meanwhile, the Donald Trump administration imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday, hours after former court judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote international law.US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the sanctions were intended to prevent the ICC from prosecuting American citizens. The move marks a further escalation in the administration’s campaign against the Hague-based court.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump slams Norway for not awarding him the Nobel Peace Prize. Trump claims he deserved the honour eight times for the wars he said he had settled. He also claimed to have saved 50 million lives by preventing India and Pakistan from going to war.

Article Title: Alaska spent $46 million to lower power bills for 81,000 people in 188 rural communities, many reliant on diesel
Article Text:
PC: AI Generated

How did Alaska spend about $46 million to lower electricity costs

Alaska’s endowment fund helps finance rural electricity support

How does Alaska’s Power Cost Equalization programme help rural customers

How can modern fuel facilities help lower energy costs in rural Alaska

Alaska Energy Authority disbursed about $46 million in Power Cost Equalization payments during fiscal year 2025 to help reduce electricity costs for rural residents and community facilities across the state. The programme serves more than 81,000 Alaskans in 188 primarily diesel-dependent communities, with customers in 186 communities benefiting from PCE credits.According to the 2025 AEA Annual Report (Alaska Energy Authority), the payments support rural residents while also helping the long-term viability of utilities serving Alaska’s most remote communities. AEA administers the programme by providing payments to eligible rural electric utilities, which apply credits to qualifying residential and community facility customers. The programme was established in 1984 to bring rural electricity costs closer to those paid in Alaska’s larger cities.The Power Cost Equalization Program was established in 1984 to reduce electricity costs for rural residents and community facilities to levels comparable to those paid in Alaska’s larger cities.AEA administers the programme for more than 81,000 Alaskans in 188 primarily diesel-dependent communities.Residential and community facility customers in 186 communities benefit from PCE credits. AEA calculates payments using monthly utility filings and disburses the money to eligible utilities.The utilities then apply credits to qualifying customers for electricity use up to specified consumption limits. In fiscal year 2025, AEA disbursed about $46 million in PCE payments to rural utilities. The payments help ease electricity costs for residents and community facilities while supporting long-term viability of utilities serving remote communities.PCE payments are funded by the PCE Endowment Fund. Alaska Statute 42.45.085 authorises the Legislature to appropriate up to five percent of the fund’s three-year average market value for PCE payments.In recent years, the five-percent draw has fully funded PCE disbursements. Statutory changes enacted in fiscal year 2018 established how excess earnings are allocated. These changes allow endowment earnings to fully cover PCE programme administrative costs and direct $30 million annually to the Community Assistance Program.The statute also authorises up to $25 million to support the Renewable Energy Fund, Rural Power System Upgrade projects, and the Alaska Division of Community and Regional Affairs’ Bulk Fuel Revolving Loan Fund.The programme provides different electricity credit limits for residential customers and public facilities. Residential customers may receive PCE credit for up to 750 kilowatt-hours per month. Community facilities may receive PCE credit of 70 kilowatt-hours per month multiplied by the number of residents.The programme works through eligible rural electric utilities, which receive payments from AEA and apply credits to qualifying customers. In many rural communities, electricity rates before PCE exceed urban rates. AEA’s PCE team also provides technical assistance to utility clerks to support accurate reporting and filing. This administration allows the programme to calculate and distribute payments based on monthly utility filings while maintaining the credit structure for participating customers and community facilities across rural Alaska.Rural Alaska relies heavily on diesel fuel for power generation and heating, and many villages depend on barges to deliver fuel for diesel-fired generators and heating. The annual report says rural energy infrastructure also includes bulk fuel facilities that can be more than 40 years old and may exceed their useful life or not meet current standards.AEA’s Rural Power Systems Upgrade and Bulk Fuel Upgrade programmes address parts of this infrastructure. The report says modern facilities can lower energy costs by preventing leaks and failures, while bulk storage allows communities to purchase fuel in larger quantities.
Article Summary: Alaska Energy Authority disbursed about $46 million in Power Cost Equalization payments during fiscal year 2025. The programme serves more than 81,000 Alaskans in 188 primarily diesel-dependent communities, with customers in 186 communities benefiting from PCE credits. The payments help ease electricity costs for residents and community facilities.

Article Title: Texas businessman spent years turning King Ludwig II’s unrealised castle plans into a 110-acre estate; his Falkenstein Castle is now listed for $9 million
Article Text:
Representative Image of a majestic Texas castle inspired by Ludwig II’s unrealized plans, surrounded by scenic Hill Country landscapes (AI Generated Image)

Neuschwanstein Castle, King Ludwig II and the plans that inspired the Texas castle

Falkenstein Castle in Burnet: 14,000 square feet, seven bedrooms and six tiny homes

Falkenstein Castle price history: from $15 million to $9 million

Ludwig II's castles gained UNESCO World Heritage status in 2025

A castle inspired by the unrealised plans of Bavarian King Ludwig II is on the market in the Texas Hill Country. Falkenstein Castle in Burnet sits on 110 acres and contains a roughly 14,000-square-foot stone residence with seven bedrooms, six tiny homes and an additional apartment above a maintenance garage. The property is currently listed for $9 million, after first being offered for $15 million in May 2025 and going through a series of price reductions. The castle was built by Texas businessman Terry Young and his wife, Kim, after a 1995 trip to Germany's Neuschwanstein Castle. According to the couple's own account of the project, drawings for another castle planned by Ludwig II inspired them to build their own version in Texas. Young has since died, and press reports say the property was passed to the couple's son, who decided to put it on the market.The story began in 1995, when the Youngs travelled to Germany and visited Neuschwanstein Castle. The Bavarian Palace Administration records that the foundation stone for Neuschwanstein was laid on September 5, 1869, after work on the site had begun the previous year. The castle remained unfinished when Ludwig II died in 1886.According to the Youngs' account of their trip, they noticed drawings in a gallery at Neuschwanstein that did not appear to depict the castle they had just toured. After asking about them, they were told they related to another project Ludwig II had planned, Falkenstein. The couple's account says they later travelled to Lechbruck, Germany, to meet Wilhelm Kienberger, a former Neuschwanstein director who had the drawings, and that Kienberger made copies of Christian Jank's rendering of the planned Falkenstein along with other sketches. A later Texas Hill Country article retells the same account of the Youngs' discovery of the drawings, their meeting with Kienberger and their decision to build a Texas castle inspired by the plans.The historical basis for the story is that Ludwig II really did plan a Falkenstein castle near Pfronten in Bavaria. Historical accounts identify Christian Jank as the artist behind an 1883 design, while later designs for the site were also produced. The project was never built, although work connected with the planned site had progressed by the mid-1880s. Falkenstein therefore remained a project on paper, rather than one of Ludwig II's completed residences.The Texas project eventually became a substantial estate. Photographs taken by Carol M. Highsmith in 2014 for her archive at the Library of Congress describe Falkenstein Castle as a residence built from scratch by Kim and Terry Young in the hills below Burnet. Her captions also record the use of large quantities of limestone, granite, sand, cement, rock and block in the buildings and note that the castle was sometimes opened for weddings.Current property listings describe the estate as approximately 14,000 square feet on 110 acres, with seven bedrooms, four full bathrooms and four half bathrooms. The grounds include six tiny homes and an apartment above a maintenance garage. The listing also describes hilltop views of the Highland Lakes and presents the property as a residence, event venue or investment property. The MLS records 1998 as the year built. The Texas castle is not a reconstruction of an existing medieval German building. It is a modern residence whose design was inspired by Ludwig II's planned Falkenstein project and the Youngs' experience visiting Neuschwanstein. The Library of Congress archive's 2014 photographs provide a contemporary record of the completed Texas property.The property's asking price has changed substantially since it first went on the market. The property was initially offered for $15 million in May 2025. It was subsequently reduced to $14 million and later to $9 million. The exact dates of the reductions have been reported differently across property coverage, so the safest figure to use is the current $9 million asking price and the documented $15 million starting price rather than presenting an uncertain day-by-day price history.At $9 million, the asking price works out to roughly $643 per square foot based on the 14,000-square-foot figure in the property listing, before accounting for the 110 acres, six tiny homes and an additional apartment. The sale follows the death of Terry Young. Press reports say the property was passed down to the Youngs' son, who subsequently decided to sell it. That gives the current listing a different context from the castle's original construction: the property that began as the couple's response to a German architectural idea is now being offered to a new owner.There is also a recent historical connection to the story. In July 2025, UNESCO inscribed The Palaces of King Ludwig II of Bavaria: Neuschwanstein, Linderhof, Schachen and Herrenchiemsee on the World Heritage List. Neuschwanstein is therefore now part of a four-site UNESCO property associated with Ludwig II. Falkenstein, the separate castle he planned but never built, is not part of that UNESCO inscription. The Texas Falkenstein stands apart from those historic Bavarian palaces. It was built more than a century after Ludwig II's death, on a hilltop in Burnet rather than in Bavaria, but its design traces back to the plans for a castle that the Bavarian king never got to build. The 110-acre property is now being offered for $9 million, giving the unfinished 19th-century vision a modern Texas chapter.
Article Summary: Falkenstein Castle in Burnet, Texas, was built by Terry and Kim Young after a 1995 trip to Germany's Neuschwanstein Castle. According to the couple's own account of the project, drawings for another castle planned by Ludwig II inspired them to build their own version in Texas. The property is currently listed for $9 million, after first being offered for $15 million in May 2025 and going through a series of price reductions.

Article Title: 'Things going to get treacherous': Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida as Category 2 storm
Article Text:
Hurricane Isaias has made its presence felt near Destin, Florida, registering maximum sustained winds of 105 mph.

Hurricane Isaias has made landfall near Destin, Florida, with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (165 kph), according to the US National Hurricane Center (NHC), Reuters reported on Friday. The storm is located about 50 miles (80 km) west-northwest of Panama City, Florida, the agency said in its latest advisory.The landfall comes as coastal communities across Florida's Panhandle and parts of Alabama prepare for damaging winds, flooding and a potentially life-threatening storm surge. Earlier forecasts warned that water levels could rise by 6 to 9 feet in vulnerable coastal areas.“Things are going to get really, really treacherous over the next couple hours,” Jamie Rhome, deputy director of the National Hurricane Center, said earlier, according to the Associated Press (AP).Authorities have issued hurricane warnings from Ocean Springs in Mississippi to the western Florida Panhandle, while several counties have ordered mandatory evacuations. Mobile, Alabama, has also imposed a curfew as officials prepare for the storm's impact.More than 365,000 customers in Florida and Alabama were without electricity on Friday evening, according to poweroutage.com. Officials in Mobile reported fallen trees and power lines, while the Emerald Coast Utilities Authority issued a boil-water notice for some customers in Florida.Florida Governor Ron DeSantis warned residents to prepare for power outages, fuel shortages and the possible closure of bridges and highways. The state's National Guard deployed around 5,000 soldiers and airmen to support emergency operations, while search-and-rescue teams were placed on standby. Some prisons also evacuated inmates.Residents have been securing their homes and filling sandbags to limit potential flood damage. In Panama City, people braved heavy rain to protect their properties ahead of the storm.Anne Petzold, a resident of Gulf Breeze, said she and her husband had installed hurricane shutters and cleared their yard of objects that could become dangerous in high winds.“Everybody does what they can do, everybody asks if they need help — they ask for help, they offer help. All good,” she said. “It's just another adventure.”The NHC has forecast 4 to 8 inches of rainfall, with localised totals potentially reaching 15 inches in parts of the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama and southwestern Georgia. The storm is expected to weaken as it moves inland, but flooding and hazardous weather could continue across parts of the southeastern US.
Article Summary: Hurricane Isaias has made landfall near Destin, Florida, with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (165 kph) The storm is located about 50 miles (80 km) west- northwest of Panama City, Florida. Authorities have issued hurricane warnings from Ocean Springs in Mississippi to the western Florida Panhandle, while several counties have ordered mandatory evacuations.

Article Title: California buried about 270,000 waste tyres beneath a highway near Confusion Hill; the rubber became lightweight fill for two new bridges
Article Text:
Image(s): Canva

Confusion Hill's rockslides had threatened US 101 for years

Engineers needed a fill material that would not overload the ground

The project used approximately 270,000 waste tyres (Image: Canva)

About 270,000 waste tyres went beneath the highway

The project showed how old tyres can become infrastructure material

A California highway project found an unusual use for thousands of discarded tyres. In 2009, the California Department of Transportation completed a road repair project at Confusion Hill on US 101 in Mendocino County, where longstanding rockslides had repeatedly threatened the highway. The new route bypassed the unstable area using two bridges, but engineers faced another problem, adding conventional fill would have placed too much weight on an underground drainage structure beneath one bridge embankment. Instead, they turned to tyre-derived aggregate (TDA), made from shredded waste tyres, as a lightweight fill material. The project ultimately used about 270,000 waste tyres, giving the discarded rubber a structural role beneath the road.The Confusion Hill project addressed a longstanding problem along US 101 near Piercy in Mendocino County. According to CalRecycle, rockslides had occurred in the area for thousands of years and had affected the highway for at least 17 years before the project. Roadway slip-outs had become more frequent, while falling debris and slope movement caused repeated closures and maintenance problems. In 2001 alone, roadway stabilisation work cost $3.2 million.Engineers needed a more reliable route through the slide area that would keep US 101 open to traffic. The solution was to bypass the unstable section with two new bridges rather than continue relying on repeated repairs to the existing route.The bridge route created a separate engineering challenge. CalRecycle says the north bridge embankment sat above an existing underground drainage structure that could not handle the additional load created by raising the embankment. Engineers therefore needed a material that could provide the necessary fill while adding less weight than conventional soil or rock. Tire-derived aggregate was selected for the job because it is lightweight and cost-effective. TDA is produced by processing waste tyres into pieces of rubber and is used in civil engineering applications including road repairs, embankments and slope stabilisation. TDA can weigh about one-third as much as soil and other similar construction materials, making it useful where excessive loading could cause problems.For the Confusion Hill project, the existing fill material over the underground structures was removed and replaced with lightweight tire-derived aggregate. CalRecycle also records that the project used approximately 270,000 waste tyres and was completed in 2009. The tyres were not simply buried whole; they were processed into TDA and used as engineered fill within the road project. The work was a lightweight-fill project for rockslide and road repair, with the TDA incorporated into the embankment stabilisation. This turned a large quantity of waste tyres into a construction material while addressing the weight limitations around the drainage structure beneath the bridge embankment.Confusion Hill became one example of California's wider use of tire-derived aggregate in civil engineering. TDA is a material that can be used for lightweight fill behind retaining walls, road repairs and embankment construction, as well as for drainage and vibration mitigation. Its lightweight and free-draining properties can make it useful where conventional fill would create excessive loads or other engineering difficulties. The state's project profiles include other applications involving hundreds of thousands of waste tyres. Rather than sending every discarded tyre to disposal, projects such as Confusion Hill demonstrate how processed rubber can become part of infrastructure. CalRecycle continues to support TDA as a recycled material for engineering projects across California.
Article Summary: California highway project used 270,000 waste tyres. The project addressed longstanding rockslides along US 101. Conventional fill would have placed too much weight on an underground drainage structure. Tire-derived aggregate (TDA) was selected because it is lightweight and cost-effective.

Article Title: More than 150 wrestlers join Memphis battle royal for animal shelters; WWE star Jordynne Grace gives all meet-and-greet money to sanctuary
Article Text:
A memorial event for Sycho Sid

More than 150 wrestlers joined the battle royal

Jordynne Grace gave her meet-and-greet money to a sanctuary

The fundraiser was linked to Eudy’s love of animals

Sid Eudy became a major wrestling star

More than 150 wrestlers joined a huge battle royal in Memphis, Tennessee, as part of the first annual Sycho Sid Memorial Benefit, an event created to honour late wrestling star Sid Eudy, better known as Sycho Sid. The memorial combined professional wrestling with an animal-rescue fundraiser, bringing together performers from different generations and promotions. The event was held at Minglewood Hall on August 29, 2026, with proceeds from the benefit intended to support animal shelters. WWE star Jordynne Grace also appeared at the event for a meet-and-greet and pledged all the money from it to FurGiven Animal Sanctuary. The charity-focused gathering reflected Eudy’s reported love of animals while bringing a large section of the wrestling community together in his memory.The Sycho Sid Memorial Benefit was organised to remember Eudy, who died in August 2024 at the age of 63 after battling cancer. The event took place in Memphis, a city closely connected to Eudy’s wrestling career. He began wrestling professionally in the Memphis area during the 1980s before going on to become one of the biggest stars of his generation.His family helped organise the memorial, which combined wrestling matches and appearances with fundraising for animal welfare.One of the main attractions was a battle royal featuring more than 150 wrestlers. The unusually large field brought together performers from different generations and wrestling backgrounds. Names associated with the event included Carlito, Jonathan Gresham, Doug Gilbert and Tommy Rich. Jordynne Grace was also among the wrestling personalities involved. The massive battle royal gave the memorial a distinctive spectacle while helping bring attention to the event’s fundraising purpose.Grace’s appearance provided a separate and particularly unusual charity angle. The WWE star announced that all money from her meet-and-greet would go to FurGiven Animal Sanctuary. The Memphis-area organisation is a privately funded, no-kill animal rescue that works with dogs and provides support including veterinary care, training and rehabilitation. Grace’s contribution was specifically tied to her meet-and-greet. It does not mean that all wrestlers at the event donated their personal appearance fees or earnings to the sanctuary.Animal rescue was an important part of the memorial’s purpose because of Eudy’s reported affection for animals. His son, Gunnar Eudy, said when the benefit was announced that profits from the show and future events would support animal shelters in Crittenden County, Arkansas. Eudy was from West Memphis, Arkansas, located just across the Mississippi River from Memphis. His family said he particularly loved dogs and cats, giving the animal-rescue fundraiser a personal connection to the wrestler being remembered.Eudy rose to prominence in professional wrestling during the late 1980s and 1990s. He competed under several names, including Sid Vicious, Sid Justice and Sycho Sid. He won the WWF Championship twice and the WCW World Heavyweight Championship twice. He also headlined WrestleMania twice. His career made him one of the most recognisable wrestlers of his era, while his early connection to Memphis made the city a natural setting for a memorial celebrating his life and career.
Article Summary: Sycho Sid Memorial Benefit was held in Memphis, Tennessee, on August 29, 2026. More than 150 wrestlers took part in a huge battle royal. WWE star Jordynne Grace pledged all the money from her meet-and-greet to FurGiven Animal Sanctuary.

Article Title: ‘No contact, no update’: Imran Khan’s son says father silent for 6 months, aunts remain ‘abducted’
Article Text:
Imran Khan's son warns against Adiala jail protest

Kasim says protests will continue

Sisters detained ahead of PTI protest

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan’s son Kasim Khan has claimed that his three aunts remain “abducted” by Pakistani authorities, saying their family and lawyers have received no information about their condition or the reasons for their detention. He also said he and his brother have had no contact with their father for more than six months.Kasim Khan made the remarks on Thursday, weeks after his aunts Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) planned September 27 protest and march to Islamabad.The demonstrations were called to demand updates on Imran Khan's health and his release from Adiala Jail, where the former prime minister has been incarcerated since August 2023.In a post on X, Kasim Khan linked the continued detention of his aunts with the lack of contact with his father."Currently, my Aunties are still abducted. Family and lawyers have received no update on how they are, nor why they are incarcerated. Concerning my father, there is complete silence. My brother and I have had no contact with him for more than six months. We do not even know the true state of his health," the post read.Kasim Khan also referred to protests being held in Pakistan over his father's imprisonment, saying people were continuing to demand justice and the right to be heard."Meanwhile, thousands of Pakistanis are peacefully taking to the streets to protest against his illegal and politically motivated imprisonment. However, the people of Pakistan have not given up. No barricade, intimidation or repression can muzzle the people’s demand for justice and their democratic right to be heard. There can be no lasting peace or stability while their democratic will is suppressed and their chosen leader remains behind bars,” Kasim Khan added.His remarks came a day after the families of the three detained sisters approached the Lahore High Court seeking permission for relatives and lawyers to meet them.According to Dawn, Advocate Rana Mudassar Umar filed two civil miscellaneous applications in pending writ petitions on behalf of Shah Raiz Khan, son of Aleema Khan, and Sakeena Niazi, daughter of Noreen Niazi.The pleas challenged the denial of meetings between the detained women and their family members and lawyers, and also raised the issue of access to medicines.The families have alleged that neither relatives nor legal counsel have been permitted to meet the three women or provide them with medicines. The applications stated that medicines had been provided to the sisters on only one occasion and that no one had subsequently been allowed to meet them, Dawn reported.The pleas have sought directions from the Lahore High Court allowing family members and lawyers to meet the detained women and provide them with medicines, according to Dawn.Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were detained for 30 days ahead of PTI's September 27 protest call.The detentions came amid a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its planned countrywide demonstrations and march to Islamabad. The party had called for the protests to demand Imran Khan's release and mobilise support for the supremacy of the Constitution.On September 24, the Lahore High Court had declined a request to immediately suspend notifications ordering the preventive detention of the three sisters.Imran Khan has been in Adiala Jail since August 2023. His detention and the PTI's protests have remained at the centre of a wider political confrontation in Pakistan, with the party continuing to demand his release.
Article Summary: Kasim Khan claims his three aunts remain 'abducted' by Pakistani authorities. He also says he and his brother have had no contact with their father for six months. His aunts Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) planned September 27 protest.

Article Title: Pak army chief Munir bypasses PM Sharif, moves to deploy more military assets to Saudi Arabia
Article Text:
Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is built on on a 2025 Saudi-Pakistani pact under which Pakistan had sent about 8,000 troops to the kingdom by May (Photo: Agencies).

Pakistan defence forces chief Asim Munir agreed to quickly deploy more Pakistani troops to Saudi Arabia , despite the Pakistani Parliament voting to stay out of the Houthi conflict 11 years ago.The Mecca defence pact signed by Pakistan with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August was invoked for the first time on Monday, amid increasing Houthi attacks on the Saudi kingdom.According to Reuters, the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is based on a 2025 Saudi-Pakistani pact under which Pakistan had sent about 8,000 troops to the kingdom by May.Pakistan's information ministry said the alliance "has gone through all necessary government procedures".However, it did not clarify if the cabinet or parliament was involved, calling details of the deployment "a matter ​of operational confidentiality."Senior fellow for South Asia at the Atlantic ​Council, Michael Kugelman, told Reuters that Pakistan is currently in a different era, with a comparatively weaker parliament."There were times in the past when Pakistan's parliament would vote not to send ⁠troops, and the military would abide by that decision. But it's a different era now," Kugelman said.Pakistan's armed forces have often been accused of holding the reins of Islamabad’s politics.In 2025, Munir was elected as the field marshal, the chief of all defence forces in Pakistan. Constitutional changes have allowed him to hold the position till 2030, with lifetime rank as the field marshal.Munir is also immune to any criminal prosecution, signalling the military's increasing influence over the constitutional establishment.Munir is widely acknowledged to be more powerful domestically than any of his predecessors. The military has control over major government portfolios like defence and foreign relations.Jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan ’s party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), currently protesting for his release, has accused the army of dominating politics.The relationship between Imran Khan and Asim Munir has reportedly been bitter since 2019, when Munir, then director-general of Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), was removed after less than eight months in the post, reportedly at the insistence of the then-PM Khan.No official reason was given for Munir’s removal.Khan was himself ousted as prime minister in April 2022. Seven months later, in November 2022, Munir returned to the centre of Pakistan’s power structure when PM Shehbaz Sharif appointed him army chief, succeeding Bajwa.
Article Summary: Pakistan's armed forces have often been accused of holding the reins of Islamabad’s politics. Mecca defence pact signed by Pakistan with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August was invoked for the first time on Monday. Pakistan's information ministry said the alliance "has gone through all necessary government procedures"

Article Title: Pakistan bets on electric vehicles as Middle East war sends petrol prices soaring 54%
Article Text:
Pakistan fuel prices to be revised every day

Poll Vote & Share your view How do rising oil prices influence your view on transitioning to electric vehicles? Strongly encourage me to switch Have no impact on my decision 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

EV sales accelerate amid fuel price pressure

Pakistan expects to achieve its electric-vehicle adoption target ahead of schedule as surging oil prices make the shift away from petrol-powered vehicles increasingly attractive, a senior government official said.The government aims for electric vehicles to account for 30% of new vehicle sales by 2030 under its EV policy announced last year. Haroon Akhtar, adviser to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on industries and production, said the sharp rise in fuel prices has reduced the time needed for buyers to recover the higher upfront cost of EVs.“I feel that the target we had set in our electric-vehicle policy last year, we will achieve it much earlier as rise in oil prices has brought cost recovery of EV to one to one and a half year,” Akhtar told Bloomberg in Islamabad.“People are realizing the benefit now. You don't have to pay for petrol,” he said.Petrol and diesel prices in Pakistan have risen 54% and 43%, respectively, since the Middle East conflict began in February, according to data available from Pakistan State Oil Company Ltd.Akhtar said sales of electric motorcycles and scooters have tripled from a year earlier, while electric-car sales have doubled, although industry-wide EV sales data is not publicly available.“This is an impact of the Middle East conflict, as fuel prices have gone up,” Akhtar said.Despite the growing incentive to switch to EVs, factors including high vehicle costs and limited charging infrastructure mean a large-scale transformation of Pakistan’s vehicle fleet and oil consumption will take years.The government is also preparing a new auto policy that could be presented to the cabinet within the next two weeks. It is considering tax incentives for EVs to narrow the price gap between electric and conventional vehicles, Akhtar said.
Article Summary: Pakistan aims for electric vehicles to account for 30% of new vehicle sales by 2030. The sharp rise in fuel prices has reduced the time needed for buyers to recover the higher upfront cost of EVs. The government is also preparing a new auto policy that could be presented to the cabinet within the next two weeks.

Article Title: Pakistan forces accused of quadcopter blast that killed 2 children in Balochistan
Article Text:
Pakistan forces accused of quadcopter link

A blast in Balochistan's Panjgur district killed two children and left three others injured, The Balochistan Post reported. The incident took place in Fateh Ali Bazaar in Gowargo tehsil, where the children had been playing.According to the report, the children noticed an unidentified object hanging from a tree. The object exploded after it was disturbed, killing two boys aged nine and 10. Three other boys, aged seven, nine and 12, were injured.The nature of the device that caused the explosion remains unclear.However, local sources alleged that it was connected to a quadcopter operated by Pakistani security forces. One source also claimed that explosives had been attached to a military quadcopter and placed in the area.The source further alleged that local journalists were later told to describe the incident as a hand-grenade blast or an explosion involving another device.The Panjgur incident comes amid other allegations of civilian casualties involving military drones and quadcopters in Balochistan.On September 24, four young men were killed and two others injured in an alleged military drone strike in Balicha, Kech, according to The Balochistan Post.Families of those killed said the men had gone there for a picnic and denied claims that they were militants.The incident triggered a boycott of courts across Makran, while lawyers called for an independent probe into the deaths.Earlier on September 18, five civilians were reportedly injured in alleged quadcopter attacks in Balochabad and Bullo in the Mand area, the report said.
Article Summary: Blast in Balochistan's Panjgur district killed two children and left three others injured. Local sources alleged that it was connected to a quadcopter operated by Pakistani security forces. Incident comes amid other allegations of civilian casualties involving military drones and quadcopters.

Article Title: Nearly 3 in 4 Pakistan inmates await trial amid prison overcrowding in country: Report
Article Text:
73% of Pakistan prisoners are under-trial, HRCP report finds

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the main cause of prison overcrowding in Pakistan? Delays in the justice system Arbitrary arrests Weak bail procedures Other reasons 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan's prisons are facing severe overcrowding, with people awaiting trial making up nearly three-fourths of the country's prison population, a Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) report has found.The report, 'Beyond the Prison Wall: Reducing Overcrowding in Pakistan's Prisons', said 73.41% of inmates were under-trial in 2024. The share has gone up from 66% in 2017, The Express Tribune reported.The report said Pakistan's prisons were operating at 152.2% of their approved capacity on average during July and August 2024.The HRCP said simply building more prisons would not address the problem. It pointed to delays in the justice system, including lengthy trials, weak bail procedures and the widespread use of pre-trial detention.Punjab faces an even bigger problem. According to official figures cited by the HRCP, 74,773 prisoners were held in 45 prisons across the province in September 2026. The sanctioned capacity was 39,204, meaning the prisons were operating at nearly 191% of capacity.Of the total inmates, 54,932 were awaiting trial.Punjab has added new prisons, barracks and other facilities over the years, but the report said the additional capacity has not matched the rise in the number of prisoners.The scale of the problem has grown majorly. Punjab province had 52,803 prisoners against a capacity of 21,527 in 2010. Overcrowding in the province stood at 173.6% in 2024, according to figures cited by The Express Tribune.The HRCP blamed arbitrary arrests, delays in investigations and lengthy prosecution for the growing number of people held without conviction.As a result, many accused people remain behind bars for months or even years while waiting for investigations and court proceedings to move forward, the report said.
Article Summary: 73.41% of inmates in Pakistan's prisons were under-trial in 2024. The share has gone up from 66% in 2017, according to a Human Rights Commission of Pakistan report. The HRCP said simply building more prisons would not address the problem. Delays in the justice system, arbitrary arrests and weak bail procedures were blamed.

Article Title: 'Come to your senses': What is Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif's condition for talks with Imran's party
Article Text:
Shehbaz’s talks offer fails to sway PTI as long march presses on

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think dialogue is the best way to resolve political disagreements? Yes, dialogue can help No, other steps are needed It depends on the situation 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Imran Khan-led Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Tuesday questioned the seriousness of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s offer for talks, calling it "merely symbolic" and saying the government had taken no concrete step beyond extending the invitation, Pakistan Today reported.PTI spokesperson Gohar said the Shehbaz Sharif-led government had also prevented PTI leaders from meeting the party’s founder and former PM Imran Khan , for nearly a year.Speaking to reporters in Rawalpindi, he said the last such meeting took place in October last year, Geo News reported.His remarks came after Sharif asked PTI to halt its ongoing long march towards Islamabad as a condition for holding talks.At an event in Islamabad, the prime minister warned that protests and long marches could hurt Pakistan’s economy. "I urge you to come to your senses, end the long march and sit-in, and then we will sit with you," he said.The PTI-led march, meanwhile, continued towards Peshawar on Monday, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi calling on party supporters to join the mobilisation.Afridi addressed march participants after the convoy reached Kohat and thanked residents for their "magnificent welcome". He said the convoy would resume its journey towards Peshawar from University Chowk on Tuesday, The Express Tribune reported.Declaring his loyalty to Imran Khan, Afridi said, “I am a soldier of Imran Khan. Even if the whole world comes together, it cannot put a price on me." He also urged supporters to send a message that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa belongs to Imran Khan.The chief minister had started the march from Lakki Marwat on Sunday after negotiations between PTI and the federal government failed to settle differences over the planned protest.Those talks, led by national assembly speaker Ayaz Sadiq, ended on Saturday without an agreement.The Pakistan government had asked PTI to call off the march, while the opposition sought assurances that its leaders would be permitted to meet long-imprisoned Imran Khan.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif asked PTI to halt its long march towards Islamabad as a condition for holding talks. PTI spokesperson said government had taken no concrete step beyond extending invitation. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi called on supporters to join mobilisation.

Article Title: Pakistan successfully test-fires extended version of Fatah-4 cruise missile
Article Text:
Senior Pakistan army officers, together with scientists and engineers, were reportedly present to watch the launch.

Pakistan successfully test-fired its homemade extended version of the ground-based Fatah-4 cruise missile on Tuesday.The cruise missile is capable of engaging long-range targets with high precision, the army said. PTI reported.In a statement, Pakistan Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said the “weapon system is capable of engaging targets at extended ranges with high precision and lethality.”According to the Pakistan army, the test validated additional technical parameters of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability.Senior Pakistan army officers, together with scientists and engineers, were reportedly present to watch the launch.President Asif Ali Zardari , Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif , Field Marshal Asim Munir, who serves as Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, and the services chiefs praised the successful test.Pakistan had previously carried out a successful test of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile in May.The base version of Fatah-4 reportedly has a range of up to 750 kilometres and can reportedly hit targets with a five-metre accuracy.The military confirmed the new variant has an extended range but did not clarify how far.Fatah-4 is a conventional cruise missile of Islamabad’s army rocket force command. It flies at an altitude of about 50 meters to evade air defences and avoid radar detection.
Article Summary: Pakistan successfully test-fired its homemade extended version of the ground- based Fatah-4 cruise missile on Tuesday. Senior Pakistan army officers, together with scientists and engineers, were reportedly present to watch the launch. President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Field Marshal Asim Munir and the services chiefs praised the successful test.

Article Title: Another showdown brewing in Pakistan? Imran Khan supporters hit streets after talks fail
Article Text:
Supporters of imprisoned Imran Khan march towards Islamabad demanding his release.

Talks between PTI, government fail

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you feel about the government response to the PTI protests? It's appropriate and necessary. It's excessive and unjustified. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Thousands of supporters of jailed former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan began a march towards Islamabad on Sunday, demanding his release after talks between his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party and the government failed to break the political deadlock.Khan, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's main political rival, has been in prison since 2023 on corruption and other charges. Khan and his party have described the cases as politically motivated, the Associated Press reported.Despite his imprisonment, he continues to command a large and committed support base.The protesters set off from Lakki Marwat district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where PTI is in power, in a convoy of trucks, buses and cars. Organisers have planned overnight stops as the caravan makes its way towards Islamabad.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi, a staunch Khan supporter, is leading the march. Speaking from a specially designed container truck bearing a large portrait of Khan, Afridi expressed confidence that the movement would succeed in taking its demands to the heart of the capital.Authorities have erected roadblocks using shipping containers at entry points to Islamabad and at several locations inside the city.PTI and the federal government had held talks over postponing the march, but failed to reach an agreement. PTI chairman Gohar Khan said negotiations remained deadlocked after two rounds.Interior minister Mohsin Naqvi blamed Afridi for the failure of the talks and warned that he would be held responsible for any loss of life during the planned march.The government had urged PTI to postpone the protest, citing a rise in militant attacks by the Pakistani Taliban, also known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), in the northwest. The government has also accused PTI of sympathising with the TTP.PTI organisers, however, have vowed to reach Islamabad after mobilising hundreds of thousands of Khan supporters. Apart from Khan's release, protesters are demanding that he be shifted to a hospital and that his family be allowed to visit him.Officials have said Khan is in good health and receives regular family visits, but maintain that meetings with the imprisoned former prime minister cannot be used for political purposes.The march was originally scheduled for September 27 but was postponed after PTI leaders said authorities had blocked key routes to Islamabad, including the Attock Bridge, a major crossing used by convoys from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.Previous protests by Khan's supporters have turned violent. During one such protest in 2024, security personnel and civilians were killed.
Article Summary: Talks between PTI, government fail to break political deadlock. Protesters set off from Lakki Marwat district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where PTI is in power, in a convoy of trucks, buses and cars. Khan has been in prison since 2023 on corruption and other charges.

Article Title: Pakistan braces for showdown as talks collapse, Imran Khan’s party pushes ahead with march
Article Text:
Imran Khan has been incarcerated since 2023.

PTI demands access to Imran Khan

Government and PTI blame each other

Long march to begin from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the federal government negotiate further with PTI? Yes, dialogue is essential No, they should stand firm Only under certain conditions 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan’s opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party will proceed with its planned long march towards Islamabad after a second round of talks with the government ended without a deal on access to jailed former prime minister Imran Khan The negotiations began at 4 pm on Saturday and continued into the early hours of Sunday, but the two sides failed to resolve their differences. The main dispute centred on PTI’s demand for an immediate meeting with Khan, including access to his personal doctor.PTI had initially planned to start the long march on September 27 but postponed it to October 4 after the federal government introduced measures aimed at preventing the protest.The party wants an immediate meeting with Khan and has demanded that he be taken to a hospital where his personal doctors can examine him.Khan, 73, has been in jail since 2023 after being convicted in a corruption case. He is currently held at the high-security Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi.PTI has also called for the release of Khan’s sisters and other people arrested ahead of the protest. It wants a proper medical examination of Khan’s wife, Bushra Bibi, and has demanded that their legal cases be heard without interference.The government, however, insisted that PTI first cancel the protest before it would consider allowing its leaders to meet Khan, according to sources. PTI rejected that condition and wanted access to its jailed leader before deciding whether to call off the march.Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ayin-e-Pakistan leader Senator Allama Nasir Abbas said the negotiations had failed because the two sides could not agree on the roles of the federal and provincial governments in dealing with terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, as well as access to Khan.“No understanding could be reached regarding the respective roles of the province and the federal government concerning terrorism in the province, and the matter of a meeting with Imran Khan remains unresolved,” Abbas, who is also Leader of the Opposition in the Senate, said.“We endeavoured to reach a conclusion, but the deadlock persists -- specifically regarding access to Khan Sahib's personal physician,” he added.Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry said the talks failed mainly because the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government could not guarantee that it would cooperate with the federal government in the fight against terrorism in the future.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is governed by PTI, and the province is also where the planned march will begin.Pakistan Peoples Party leader Sherry Rehman, who took part in the negotiations, said the government delegation had discussed all the opposition's demands.“Unfortunately, the draft [agreement] was changed four times after it was agreed upon,” she told Geo News, adding that she would not go into the details.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi announced at 12:46 am that the protest would go ahead.He said supporters from Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan, Bannu and Lakki Marwat would join the march at Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat at 1 pm on Sunday.The convoy is scheduled to stop near Karak for the night before leaving at 12:30 pm the following day and staying overnight near Kohat.On October 6, protesters from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram and Orakzai will join the convoy as it moves towards Peshawar, with the group expected to spend the night near Mattani.Afridi said the caravan would leave Budh Bair in Peshawar on the afternoon of October 7. Supporters from other parts of Peshawar will join at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza before the convoy moves towards Charsadda.“The remaining constituencies of Peshawar will join us at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza. And we will spend the night near Charsadda Interchange,” he said.The protesters are scheduled to leave Charsadda Interchange at 12:30 pm on October 8 after supporters from Charsadda and Mohmand join them.Afridi said people from across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa would gather at Khairabad later that day before the next stage of the march is announced.“God willing, the plan for the next phase will be announced there,” he said.The federal government has warned that the protesters will not be allowed to enter Islamabad. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s political adviser Rana Sanaullah said authorities would prevent the march from reaching the capital.“No one would be allowed to enter Islamabad,” he told reporters.The government had earlier said it would block roads leading into Islamabad with shipping containers and deploy additional security personnel to prevent the protesters from entering the capital.
Article Summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party will proceed with its planned long march towards Islamabad. The party wants an immediate meeting with Khan and has demanded that he be taken to a hospital where his personal doctors can examine him. The government, however, insisted that PTI first cancel the protest before it would consider allowing its leaders to meet Khan.

Article Title: India slams Pakistan at UN, says ‘so-called’ civilian governments serve at army’s mercy
Article Text:
Pakistan's Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif

India on Friday hit back at Pakistan at the UN General Assembly, rejecting Islamabad’s remarks on Jammu and Kashmir and accusing its “so-called” civilian governments of serving “at the mercy” of the army.Exercising its Right of Reply during a Third Committee meeting, first secretary at the Permanent Mission of India to the UN Bhavika Mangalanandan said Pakistan’s civilian governments “rarely complete their terms”, while accusing Islamabad of using cross-border terrorism to divert attention from domestic discontent.Accoridng to news agency PTI, India “categorically” rejected Pakistan’s remarks on Jammu and Kashmir, asserting that the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh were, are and will always remain “integral and inalienable” parts of India.“We all know that the so-called civilian governments in Pakistan serve at the mercy of their army and rarely complete their terms,” Mangalanandan said.Referring to jailed former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan, she said a “former Prime Minister continues to remain in jail, even as his health is reported to be fast deteriorating.”She also said the erstwhile ruling party had not been allowed to contest elections.“Instead of addressing domestic discontent, Pakistan seeks to distract by fomenting instability in India and sponsoring, inciting, abetting, and financing cross-border terrorism in my country for more than three decades,” she said.Turning to Jammu and Kashmir, Mangalanandan said, “The only outstanding matter is a vacation of the territory Pakistan holds under illegal and forcible occupation.She accused Pakistan of attempting to divert attention from unrest in the country.“This is a desperate attempt by Pakistan to mask the ongoing tragedy in Rawalakot and its other cities, the killing of hundreds of civilians, and the brutal crackdown across Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, for merely demanding bread, electricity and human dignity,” she said.India also invoked the term “Form 47”, used in reference to allegations of rigging and manipulation in Pakistan’s 2024 general elections.“When any free media is banned from covering such news in Pakistan, the evidence becomes undeniable for the global community that only the writ of the Form 47 government and their masters and the army headquarters runs large,” she said.Contrasting this with Jammu and Kashmir, India said Assembly Elections were held there in 2024, followed by a peaceful transfer of power to an elected government.“The contrast could not have been starker. The only human rights violation taking place in Kashmir is perpetrated by the armed forces of Pakistan and their terrorist proxies. Propaganda does not become fact through repetition,” Mangalanandan said.“Pakistan would serve its people better by confronting its own fault lines and building its economy than by coveting the territory of others,” she added.
Article Summary: India “categorically” rejected Pakistan’s remarks on Jammu and Kashmir, asserting that the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh were, are and will always remain “integral and inalienable”

Article Title: Pakistan kills 5 TTP militants as violence escalates on Afghanistan border
Article Text:
The militants reportedly belonged to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, which the government calls Fitna al-Khawarij (Representative image: Reuters).

Pakistani security forces killed five militants during an intelligence-based operation on Saturday in the country's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.The militants reportedly belonged to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan , which the government calls Fitna al-Khawarij.The operation was carried out in KPK's South Waziristan district, based on intelligence about several militant hideouts, PTI reported, citing an official.A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was also recovered, the official said.Pak army has been targeting such hideouts amid increased violence at the Afghanistan border.On Friday, seven militants belonging to the same group were killed in North Waziristan district. Such operations form part of Pakistan's Azm-e-Istehkam initiative, aimed at countering terrorism.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has long struggled with instability, fueled by militant violence, the movement of fighters across the border from Afghanistan, and repeated military campaigns.After its ceasefire agreement with the Pakistani government collapsed in November 2022, the TTP has launched a series of attacks in the province, which borders Afghanistan.Last week, a suicide bombing at a roadside police checkpoint in KPK's Dera Ismail Khan district killed more than a dozen security personnel and wounded at least 30 others. Nearly 21 people died in the city of Kohat after a car loaded with explosives rammed into the entrance of a mosque; both attacks were linked to the TTP.According to the Centre for Research and Security Studies, an Islamabad-based think tank, KPK was Pakistan's worst-hit region for violence in the third quarter of 2025. The region recorded around 638 violence-related deaths, nearly 71 per cent of the national total. KPK also faced 221 violent incidents, more than 67 per cent of the total.Overall, Pakistan recorded 1,232 rebel group attacks during the first nine months of 2026, according to a report by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, with the number of attacks in September reaching a 12-year high.
Article Summary: Militants reportedly belonged to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, which the government calls Fitna al-Khawarij. Operation carried out in KPK's South Waziristan district, based on intelligence about several militant hideouts. A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was also recovered.

Article Title: Pakistan logs over 1.2k rebel attacks in 9 months of ’26, security crisis deepens
Article Text: During the first nine months of 2026, Pakistan recorded 1,232 rebel group attacks, according to a report by Islamabad-based think tank Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, indicating that a major security crisis is brewing. The number of attacks in Sept reached a 12-year high, with 225 attacks resulting in 545 deaths. Police and military personnel have been the primary targets of these operations, accounting for majority of fatalities.Spearheaded by groups such as Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Baloch Liberation Army, Baloch Liberation Front and alliances like Ittehad Mujahideen Pakistan, these attacks remain concentrated in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and former tribal areas. Formed in 2025, IMP is the latest threat and comprises three sub-outfits — Hafiz Gul Bahadur group (HGBG), Lashkar-e-Islam and Harakat Inqilab-e-Islami Pakistan.Just last week, over a dozen security personnel were killed and at least 30 wounded in a suicide bombing at a roadside police checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. A week before that around 21 Pakistani security personnel were killed and dozens injured in a powerful suicide bombing and subsequent firing at the police line and intelligence facility in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.The surge in Sept represents a 13% increase from 199 incidents reported in Aug, marking the third consecutive month of compounding violence.Balochistan served as the primary epicentre of the escalation, bearing the brunt of the violence with 131 recorded attacks, accounting for more than half of all nationwide incidents. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa followed with 58 attacks, while the former tribal areas recorded 34 incidents, the institute claimed. Tensions between Islamabad and Kabul have risen as Pakistan repeatedly accuses the ruling Afghan Taliban of providing safe havens and operational freedom to the TTP.
Article Summary: During the first nine months of 2026, Pakistan recorded 1,232 rebel group attacks. The number of attacks in Sept reached a 12-year high, with 225 attacks resulting in 545 deaths. Police and military personnel have been the primary targets of these operations.

Article Title: Shehbaz govt, Imran Khan’s PTI hold talks as Pakistan braces for protests
Article Text: Pakistan’s federal government and jailed former prime minister Imran Khan ’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) agreed to hold a second round of talks on Saturday, as the opposition party prepares for a long march towards Islamabad from October 4.The first round of negotiations was held on Friday in the chamber of national assembly speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, who is facilitating the dialogue amid heightened security in the capital.According to a statement issued by the National Assembly Secretariat, the participants held detailed discussions “on the prevailing political situation and exchanged views on various matters of national importance”.“The government, PPP and opposition representatives apprised each other of their respective positions and held a detailed exchange of views constructively and cordially. The participants emphasised the need to resolve national issues through dialogue and negotiations,” it said, according to news agency PTI.The second round will be held at 2 pm on Saturday in the speaker’s chamber.Sadiq said he was “only playing the role of a mediator”, adding that his office was “always open” to resolving issues through negotiations.“Parliament is the only forum where solutions to issues can be found,” he said, stressing that negotiations were the way to address political differences.PTI international spokesman Zulfiqar Bukhari said the talks were “primarily aimed at defusing the current political situation surrounding PTI’s planned march/protest toward Islamabad on October 4”.Bukhari said the party’s demands included an “immediate” meeting with Khan and a decision to take him to hospital so his personal doctors could examine him. PTI has also sought the release of Khan’s sisters and others arrested ahead of the protest, a medical check-up for his wife Bushra Bibi and proper hearings in their cases.Meanwhile, the Pakistan authorities have deployed additional police and placed shipping containers on routes into Islamabad. The blockades have already disrupted freight movement.Bukhari said the long march would begin from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat, with stops planned in Karak and Kohat on October 5 before entering Peshawar district.
Article Summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf to hold second round of talks on Saturday. Opposition party preparing for long march towards Islamabad from October 4. First round of negotiations was held on Friday in the chamber of national assembly speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq.

Article Title: 'Vague and broad': UN experts slam Pakistan's counter-terrorism laws, demand release of lawyer couple
Article Text:
UN experts demand release of Pakistani lawyers, question terror laws

United Nations human rights experts have stepped up pressure on Pakistan to release Pakistani lawyers Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha, after the married couple was rearrested on terrorism-related charges just hours after the Supreme Court granted them bail on September 17.The Office of the UN high commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) said that the latest charges relate to an earlier case dating back to March 2025, when the two lawyers were accused in connection with their participation in a protest that authorities deemed illegal.The UN experts said they had already expressed concern over the couple’s conviction in a separate case involving social media posts in which they supported local activists and criticised the military.They said the decision to invoke an older case immediately after Mazari-Hazir and Chattha secured bail “appears to be an attempt” to use the criminal justice system to punish freedom of expression and human rights advocacy.The couple’s rearrest was followed by proceedings before an Islamabad anti-terrorism court. Police had sought 30 days of custody for interrogation, but the court rejected the request and ordered that the lawyers be sent to jail on a 14-day judicial remand, OHCHR said.Their legal proceedings continued on September 22, when an Islamabad anti-terrorism court returned their bail petitions because they did not carry signed powers of attorney, according to the UN rights office.The UN experts also raised broader concerns about Pakistan’s use of counter-terrorism legislation, criticising what they described as “vague and broad” provisions that could be used to restrict human rights and interfere with legitimate advocacy.They called on Pakistani authorities to drop any charges stemming from the lawyers’ exercise of freedom of expression or their legitimate professional work.The experts also urged authorities to ensure that the couple had access to lawyers of their choice, their families and necessary medical care.The UN experts said they had been in contact with the Pakistani government over their concerns.
Article Summary: Pakistani lawyers Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha were rearrested on terrorism-related charges just hours after the Supreme Court granted them bail. The UN experts said they had already expressed concern over the couple’s conviction in a separate case involving social media posts in which they supported local activists.

Article Title: Policeman killed in gunmen attack in Pakistan’s khyber pakhtunkhwa
Article Text:
A police officer was killed in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

A police officer was killed in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province after two armed med riding a motorcycle attacked him with a hand grenede and fired at him while he was deployed outside a hospital, police said.The attack took place in the unstable province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Tank area.The banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) later claimed the responsibility for the attack, as per the PTI report.According to the police, the two attackers escaped from the spot on their motorcyclen after the attackSecurity personnel have launched a search operation to trace the assailants, while an investigation into the incident is also in progress.Over the years, there have been several instances of terrorist violence in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which shares a border with Afghanistan. The transfer of combatants across borders and subsequent military actions have also been connected to the disturbance.The TTP has continued to carry out attacks in the province since its ceasefire agreement with the Pakistani government ended in November
Article Summary: The attack took place in the unstable province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Tank area. The banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) later claimed responsibility for the attack. The TTP has continued to carry out attacks in the province since its ceasefire agreement with the Pakistani government ended in November.

Article Title: Durga Puja pandal count up in Bangladesh, Hindus say ‘reduced fear’
Article Text:
Students of Dhaka University during Mahalaya in Durga Puja festivities in 2024. (File photo)

TOI

There is cautious optimism among Bangladesh’s minority Hindu community ahead of this year’s Durga Puja. Amid reduced fear after security assurances by the govt, the number of pandals has risen to 33,851 — up 1,460 from last year.Basudeb Dhar, president of Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad (BPUP), the country’s prominent non-political, social and religious organisation representing the community, toldfrom Dhaka on Friday that they were not experiencing the same “sense of fear” which had clouded their festivities the past two years.“In the past two years, our festivities faced ban threats from some right-wing groups. There were provocative social media posts and public rallies against celebrations. This year, the situation is different. BNP-led govt wants the community to celebrate with freedom and fervour. They want to showcase Bangladesh’s diversity and rich cultural heritage before the world,” added Dhar.Dhar attended a high-level meeting chaired by home minister Salahuddin Ahmed on the security arrangements for Durga Puja, a few days ago. He also informed that govt’s Hindu Religious Welfare Trust had increased the grant for puja celebrations to Rs 5cr this year, against the previous year’s grant of Rs 4cr.Meanwhile, another BPUP member said that desecration of idols were reported from at least 11 districts last year. “This time, there’ve been four incidents so far -- in Sylhet, Rajbari, Panchagarh and Tangail districts. And the govt also promptly took necessary legal measures... Law enforcement agencies told us that their personnel will be deployed near the pandals, but organising committees should also have their volunteers to maintain a vigil,” he said, requesting anonymity.Earlier, home minister Ahmed had said: “No security risks have been reported regarding Durga Puja pandals in Bangladesh so far. Having said that, the law enforcement agencies will be on high alert with quick response protocols in place...”
Article Summary: The number of pandals has risen to 33,851 — up 1,460 from last year. “In the past two years, our festivities faced ban threats from some right-wing groups. This year, the situation is different. BNP-led govt wants the community to celebrate with freedom and fervour,” says BPUP president.

Article Title: 'Companies may face US sanctions': Sri Lanka to put ‘national interest’ first as 19 Iranian vessels seek help
Article Text:
(With AP inputs)

Sri Lanka said on Friday it would “prioritise our national interests” before providing assistance to the crews of 19 Iranian ships anchored in international waters near the island nation.The crews are facing shortages of food, water and fuel. A foreign ministry spokesperson cited the risk of US sanctions against Sri Lankan companies supplying the vessels as a key concern.The United States and Iran have been at war since February 28, when the US and Israel launched joint strikes against the Islamic Republic.“Sri Lanka will put its national interest first before considering any help, and the companies that supply ships are aware of possible secondary sanctions from the United States,” spokesperson Thushara Rodrigo told reporters, ruling out any immediate assistance to the vessels.Rodrigo clarified, however, that Sri Lanka had received no communication from the United States warning of repercussions if it decided to assist the vessels.According to Rodrigo, the ships are stationed 24 nautical miles off Sri Lanka’s coast.The Iranian Embassy said it had no information on the matter.In March, a US torpedo attack sank the Iranian naval vessel IRIS Dena in Sri Lankan waters, killing 87 sailors.The ship was returning to Iran after participating in a naval exercise at India’s invitation. A second Iranian vessel was brought to a Sri Lankan port after its crew reported technical problems.Wounded sailors were treated at Sri Lankan hospitals, while those rescued from the second vessel were safely repatriated to Iran.Sri Lanka is still recovering from an economic crisis, with both the United States and Iran serving as important trading partners. Washington played a key role in securing an International Monetary Fund bailout and supporting Sri Lanka’s agricultural sector to help avert a food crisis.
Article Summary: 19 Iranian ships anchored in international waters near Sri Lanka. Crews are facing shortages of food, water and fuel. Sri Lankan companies supplying the vessels are at risk of US sanctions. The United States and Iran have been at war since February 28.

Article Title: Makeup, colourful scarves, speaking in public: Bizarre reasons women get detained in Afghanistan
Article Text:
File photo: Taliban detain 53 over dress code

What can get women detained under Taliban rule?

A wider crackdown on women

Afghanistan’s Taliban authorities detained 52 women and one girl between July and September for alleged dress code violations and appearing in public without a male guardian, including for wearing makeup, colourful scarves or leaving their hair visible, the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) said on Thursday.The arrests were reported in Kabul and the western city of Herat. UNAMA said it was “gravely concerned” about the detentions and threats of arrest, warning that safety concerns and stigma could mean many more cases had gone unreported. It also raised alarm over reports of verbal abuse, beatings and threats against women, including female shopkeepers. The Taliban government did not immediately respond to the statement.The reasons cited in the latest cases offer a glimpse of how closely the Taliban police women’s appearance and movement in public. Women were reportedly detained for not wearing a chador, leaving their hair visible, wearing colourful scarves or makeup, or going out without a mahram, a close male relative who acts as a guardian.These restrictions sit alongside the Taliban’s 2024 Law on the Propagation of Virtue and Prevention of Vice, which lays out detailed requirements for women’s clothing and conduct.Article 13 says women must cover their entire bodies and states that they should cover their faces to prevent fitna. It also requires women to conceal their voices in certain public settings, including singing, reciting or chanting aloud in gatherings.The law further says women’s clothing must not be thin, short or tight, and that women must conceal their bodies and faces from men who are not close male relatives. It also says an adult woman leaving home for an urgent need must conceal her voice, face and body.The law applies across Afghanistan and provides for a sequence of enforcement measures, ranging from warnings and fines to detention. The translated text also allows enforcers to impose other punishments they consider appropriate, subject to the law’s stated conditions.Since returning to power in 2021, the Taliban have imposed sweeping restrictions on women and girls, including barring girls from education beyond primary school and curbing women’s movement and participation in public life.The latest detentions come months after Taliban authorities opened fire on a rare protest in Herat in June over the arrest of women for alleged dress code violations. At least one person was killed and several others were wounded, according to witnesses and UNAMA.
Article Summary: Afghanistan’s Taliban authorities detained 52 women and one girl between July and September for alleged dress code violations. The arrests were reported in Kabul and the western city of Herat. Women were reportedly detained for not wearing a chador, leaving their hair visible, wearing colourful scarves or makeup.
